Issue: Arabic-numbered headings are dropped by the digit-led guard, collapsing numbered documents to 1 chapter

## Summary

`_structural_chapter_count()` rejects any ATX title starting with a digit — a guard meant to keep `## 5 Setup` from counting as a chapter. That guard drops **every arabic-numbered heading**, which is how academic papers, technical reports and standards documents are structured, and which is exactly what `--mode technical` with Docling produces.

## Reproduction — four forms, all lost

Three same-level sections per document; the detector should see 3:

```
"## 1. Intro"    -> 1   rejected
"## 1 Intro"     -> 1   rejected
"## 1) Intro"    -> 1   rejected
"## 1.2 Intro"   -> 1   rejected
"## I. Intro"    -> 3   ok   (roman survives)
"## Intro"       -> 3   ok   (control)
```

(The 1 is the lone `#` document title surviving through the thin-document fallback.)

A first version of this issue described the defect as "numbering with a dot" and proposed accepting `\d+\.`. That is wrong: it fixes one of the four broken forms and leaves the other three exactly as they are.

## The knot

`## 5 Setup` — which the guard exists to reject — and `## 1 Intro` — which it should accept — are **syntactically identical**. No adjustment of the leading-token regex separates them, so any patch that admits the second admits the first.

What separates them is not the separator, it is the **sequence**. Structural numbering appears as a run: 1, 2, 3 at the same heading depth, starting at 1. A tutorial step numbered `## 5 Setup` normally appears without the siblings that would make it a sequence, or without starting at 1.

## Suggested direction

Decide per document, not per line:

1. Collect the digit-led titles at each depth, in document order.
2. If a depth holds three or more of them whose leading numbers form an ascending run starting at 1, treat that depth as structural numbering and count those titles as chapters, using the leading number as the chapter number.
3. Otherwise keep rejecting them, exactly as today.

That admits all four forms above without a separator whitelist, and leaves an isolated `## 5 Setup` rejected.

## Tests this needs

- Each of the four numbering forms, three sections each, counted as 3.
- `## 5 Setup` / `## 6 Teardown` with no sibling run: still rejected (this is the existing `test_bare_digit_titles_still_rejected`, which must stay green).
- A document mixing a numbered run with an unnumbered heading, to pin which depth wins.
- Roman and unnumbered headings unchanged.

## Where it came from

Converting *Prompt Design and Engineering* (Xavier Amatriain, 26 pages) through Codex with `--mode technical`. The document has 8 numbered sections; the run reported 4, and the agent had to rebuild the structure by reading headings itself. `chapters_detected` feeds Step 3's plan and the generated skill's file layout, so the wrong number does not just look wrong — it becomes the structure.

## Environment

book-to-skill v1.4.0, reproduced on current `master`. Source: PDF via Docling 2.119.0.
